```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
source(if (file.exists("supplement/report-helpers.R")) "supplement/report-helpers.R" else "report-helpers.R")
source(file.path(report_project_root(), "supplement", "interaction-report.R"))

scopes <- interaction_report_grid("training-status") |>
  mutate(
    support = lapply(path, interaction_csv, file = "status_support.csv"),
    moderation = lapply(path, interaction_csv, file = "training_interaction_contrasts.csv"),
    weights = lapply(path, interaction_csv, file = "stacking_weights.csv")
  )
```

# Scope and Analysis Hierarchy

This exploratory supplementary analysis restricts the frozen primary datasets
to resistance-training arms reporting trained or untrained participants.
Active and unreported classifications are excluded without reclassification.
Every candidate is refitted on the same restricted sample within each exposure
and outcome. Reported status replaces the original RT main effect and RT dose
interactions. Dose functions and study/arm/outcome structures follow the primary
family; age, duration and body mass remain in the corresponding adjusted models.

Fresh predictive stacking weights are estimated within each exposure/outcome
after sampling diagnostics and corrected observation-level LOO pass. Predictions
exclude random effects. Protein contrasts are paired within each posterior draw,
and moderation is the trained minus untrained difference in those contrasts.
The 0.1 baseline-SD threshold is descriptive when applied to moderation.

Status is a study-reported classification with heterogeneous definitions. These
between-study associations do not identify individual or causal training-history
effects. Physical function has only one or two trained studies and is reported
descriptively. A small estimated interaction does not establish absence of
moderation by actual training history. Dose-range support screens are descriptive
and do not establish joint age/duration/dose support.

# Empirical Support and Model Averaging

All 12 exposure–outcome ensembles met the diagnostic and reporting criteria. A moderation contrast passed the dose-range screen when at least three studies contributed to each status group and both doses lay inside the observed range for both groups.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-training-status-support
#| tbl-cap: "Study support and candidate counts for the reported training-status analyses. Supported contrasts are counted across both prediction profiles."

scopes |>
  transmute(
    Exposure = unname(interaction_exposures[exposure]),
    Outcome = unname(report_outcome_labels[outcome]),
    `Trained studies` = vapply(support, function(x) sum(x$studies[x$training_status == "trained"]), numeric(1)),
    `Untrained studies` = vapply(support, function(x) sum(x$studies[x$training_status == "untrained"]), numeric(1)),
    Candidates = vapply(weights, nrow, integer(1)),
    `Supported moderation contrasts` = vapply(moderation, function(x) sum(x$supported), integer(1))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# Dose–Response Results

Curves show outcome contrasts against the reference dose for the corresponding exposure. Shading shows 95% posterior intervals. The vertical dashed line marks the reference dose. Some plotted doses extend outside shared support, as documented in the linked tables.

```{r}
#| label: training-status-curves
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "100%"

for (exposure in names(interaction_exposures)) {
  cat("\n## ", interaction_exposures[[exposure]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  for (i in which(scopes$exposure == exposure)) {
    cat("\n### ", report_outcome_labels[[scopes$outcome[[i]]]], "\n\n", sep = "")
    path <- scopes$path[[i]]
    reference_dose <- unique(scopes$moderation[[i]]$current_dose)
    stopifnot(length(reference_dose) == 1L)
    print(training_status_curves(
      interaction_csv(path, "protein_contrasts.csv"),
      interaction_csv(path, "profiles.csv"),
      exposure,
      reference_dose
    ))
    interaction_links(scopes$relative_path[[i]], c(
      "Predictions" = "dose_response.csv",
      "Protein contrasts" = "protein_contrasts.csv",
      "Paired moderation contrasts" = "training_interaction_contrasts.csv",
      "Status support" = "status_support.csv",
      "Stacking weights" = "stacking_weights.csv"
    ))
  }
}
```

# Interpretation

No locally supported trained-minus-untrained difference in a protein contrast
met the 95% posterior-probability criterion for meaningful moderation in any
outcome or exposure family. Many supported contrasts were practically
equivalent; others remained uncertain, most notably for strength. Physical
function had no locally supported trained-versus-untrained contrast and remains
descriptive because only one or two trained studies contributed.

The completed analyses therefore do not provide clear evidence that the
protein dose-response differs meaningfully between study-reported trained and
untrained samples. This is not evidence that individual training history has
no modifying effect: status definitions were heterogeneous, status was mostly
a between-study characteristic, and trained-study support was sparse.
